item.title: Clean-Room Reverse-Engineering Findings from Stock Google Jamboard ROM
item.description: Overview This document records the clean-room interoperability findings obtained from inspecting partition backups (stock-system.img, stock-vendor.img, and stock-wifi-rp3.img) pulled from a Google Jamboard (baracus) running Google’s final End-of-Life Android 7.0 release (google/baracus/baracus:7.0/NRT1.240624.004/12020658:user/release-keys). The primary goal of this investigation was to determine how Google’s stock OS distinguished between fingers, the passive stylus, and the passive microfiber eraser (or any other eraser/palm), and why unmodified AOSP/LineageOS and mainline Linux kernels only expose basic finger touch.

item.title: Live Input Capture Findings for the Google Jamboard RAPT Touch Controller (LineageOS)
item.description: Overview These are measurements taken from a live Jamboard running lineage-22.2-20261109-NIGHTLY-baracus_tab (Android 15, kernel 4.9.141, userdebug, SELinux Enforcing), captured over Root ADB from /dev/hidraw*. They replace the size-band assumptions derived from static analysis of the stock ROM and are the basis for the classification in artifacts/jamboard/jamboard-pen-daemon.c. Captures were taken with a finger, the stock passive stylus (upright and tilted), a substitute whiteboard eraser (the official Jamboard eraser was not available), the heel of a palm, and the stylus with a palm resting beside it. About 34,100 contact rows were analyzed. Small derived artifacts are in artifacts/jamboard/captures/: both HID report descriptors (raw and decoded) and phase-summary.csv. The multi-megabyte raw captures were not committed.

item.title: RAPT Optical Touch/Stylus HID & MStar Scaler UART Protocol Guide
item.description: Overview This guide provides the complete wire-level protocol specification and Linux/Android integration setup for the Google Jamboard’s two custom carrier-board subsystems: RAPT Touch (“HazelRed” / hazeldos) Optical InGlass Digitizer: GPIO SPIFI power-up sequence, USB HID Report 0xF1 frame specification (basic 340-byte and extended 484-byte interfaces), live capture workflow on LineageOS, and uinput stylus/eraser translation (jamboard-pen-daemon). MStar MST9U23T1 Display Scaler (/dev/ttyTHS1): 9600-baud UART packet framing, XOR checksum algorithm, backlight brightness control, external HDMI/USB-C DisplayPort input switching, and speaker mute control (jamboard-scaler.sh). Prerequisites Unlocked Google Jamboard (baracus) running either LineageOS 22 (baracus_tab) with Root ADB or Fedora Workstation (aarch64). Companion scripts and C source from artifacts/jamboard/: artifacts/jamboard/rapt-live-probe.sh artifacts/jamboard/jamboard-pen-daemon.c artifacts/jamboard/jamboard-scaler.sh artifacts/jamboard/systemd/* Part 1: RAPT Optical Touchscreen & Stylus/Eraser Subsystem 1.1 GPIO Power-Up & SPIFI Boot Sequence The internal RAPT Touch controller (VID:PID 1cbe:0003 on Jamboard; 2986:0137 on generic RAPT firmware) is wired to internal Tegra XUSB port usb2-3 (usb-70090000.xusb-4). item.title: Chaining GitHub Actions Workflows Without a PAT or GitHub App
item.description: How to trigger one workflow from another when you can’t (or don’t want to) use Personal Access Tokens or GitHub Apps. The Problem You have two workflows: Workflow A — Detects branches and auto-creates PRs against main Workflow B — Runs tests on PRs opened against main Manual PRs trigger Workflow B. But when Workflow A creates a PR, Workflow B never runs.

item.title: HCL BigFix Agent Architecture Guide
item.description: Overview HCL BigFix is a multi-platform endpoint management platform that enables IT operations and security teams to discover, manage, patch, and secure global IT estates. Whether operating on-premises, in the cloud, or in hybrid environments, BigFix uses a unique single-agent, hierarchical architecture to manage thousands of devices efficiently with minimal bandwidth overhead.

item.title: Installing Podman on MacOS
item.description: Podman Desktop is the graphical front end for Podman on macOS. Containers do not run natively on macOS — Podman launches a lightweight Linux VM (a Podman machine) and runs containers inside it. The desktop app handles onboarding, machine management, and optional Docker compatibility so existing Docker workflows keep working. This guide covers installation, first-run setup, Docker compatibility, rootless vs rootful mode, and common gotchas — including the krunkit abort trap failure on Homebrew installs.

item.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit & CDI Setup on Proxmox GPU Passthrough VMs
item.description: Overview NVIDIA Container Toolkit with CDI (Container Device Interface) enables Docker containers to access physical GPUs. On Proxmox VMs with GPU PCI passthrough, CDI specs must be explicitly generated and Docker must be configured to use them. Prerequisites Proxmox VM with NVIDIA GPU PCI passthrough configured (IOMMU, vfio-pci) NVIDIA driver installed and nvidia-smi working on the host Docker installed Step-by-Step 1. Install NVIDIA Container Toolkit curl -fsSL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/gpgkey | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/nvidia-container-toolkit-keyring.gpg curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/deb/nvidia-container-toolkit.list | \ sed 's#deb https://#deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/nvidia-container-toolkit-keyring.gpg] https://#g' | \ sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.list sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit 2. item.title: Using the integrated OpenShift container image registry
item.description: OpenShift ships with a cluster-internal container registry (the Image Registry Operator, namespace openshift-image-registry). You can push images there instead of an external registry (for example Quay.io), as long as workloads that need the image can pull from the namespace where the image lives. This is the same pattern NVIDIA documents for hosting built images (for example vGPU Manager) on the cluster’s own registry. What you get In-cluster pull hostname (from any pod on the cluster): image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 Full image reference: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/<project>/<image>:<tag> Example: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/nvidia-gpu-operator/vgpu-manager:9.0.0.0 Private by default: images are not public on the internet; access is via Kubernetes RBAC and image pull credentials where needed.
